questions.question: Does T-cell polarization toward TH2/TFH2 and TH17/TFH17 separate IgG4-RD from healthy controls and from pSS?
Are the major lymphocyte subsets (T, CD4+, CD8+, NK, B) abnormal in IgG4-RD, or is pSS the lymphopenic group?
Does stimulated cytokine release (IL-4, IL-10, IL-17, IFNγ) differ between the three groups?
Does IFNγ release differ between IgG4-RD, HC and pSS?
Are circulating plasmablasts expanded in IgG4-RD relative to healthy controls, and is that expansion specific versus pSS?
Are regulatory T cells (CD4+FoxP3+) increased in IgG4-RD?
Is total PD1+ TFH increased in IgG4-RD, and do both representations agree?
Is TFH2 expanded in IgG4-RD in both percentage of TFH and absolute count?
Is TFH1 reduced in IgG4-RD — and does the answer depend on whether it is read as a share of TFH or as an absolute count?
Is TFH17 raised in IgG4-RD — and does the representation flip the answer in the opposite direction to TFH1?

What can be said about the patients who have no post-treatment timepoint?
Do the treated patients differ at baseline from the untreated ones?
How many patients have complete data across all four primary datasets?
Does age or sex confound the group comparisons, given that the three cohorts differ on both?
Does circulating TFH2 correlate with serum IgG4?

Does that correlation hold if the two most extreme points are removed?
Does the IgG4-RD Responder Index correlate with any measured immunological variable?

Does the IL-10 correlation reported in the figure agree with the value reported in the table?

Do patients with storiform fibrosis differ immunologically from those without?

How much of the variance in the immunological measures is explained by site or batch rather than by disease?

Do any child populations exceed their parent in comparable units?

Does the recomputed mean serum IgG4 match the published value?
Does the proportion of patients with two or more organs involved depend on how the free-text organ field is parsed?
